audit.whatIsWrong: Assassin's Mark is described as stacking 'off her own Q and any auto' (early) and 'activates on her own Q' (whys[0]), and as 'passive Mark + auto burst trades' (spikes[0]). Two later strings call her burst 'R+E+empowered Q'.
audit.why: Assassin's Mark is created by SPELL damage only — basic attacks do not create it — and it does not stack. It draws a ring around the target; Akali has to EXIT that ring to empower her next attack, which then gains bonus range and damage. That exit is the visible tell a Teemo can play around, and it is currently missing. The empowered hit is also a basic attack, so Blinding Dart cancels it outright — the single strongest piece of tech in this lane and nowhere in the entry. 'Empowered Q' is not a thing; the empowerment lands on her auto.
audit.corrected: Assassin's Mark: spell damage draws a ring, Akali exits the ring, her next basic attack gains range and damage. Blind that attack — Blinding Dart removes it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akali.json — P Assassin's Mark: 'Dealing spell damage to a champion creates a ring of energy around them. Exiting that ring empowers Akali's next Attack with bonus range and damage.' flags: autoReset

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid section states 'Twilight Shroud has a real 25-second cooldown you can exploit'. Nothing anywhere gives Shuriken Flip's cooldown, and the entry never states what Twilight Shroud actually does to Blinding Dart.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud is 20/19/18/17/16 — 20s at rank 1, not 25s. Five seconds of imagined downtime is exactly the kind of error that gets a Teemo killed walking up on a shroud he thinks is still down. Separately, untargetability means Blinding Dart cannot be cast on her at all while she is in the smoke (Q is a targeted single-target spell), whereas poison and mushroom damage already applied keep ticking — the entry gets the second half right in 'late' but never states the first half. Shuriken Flip is 16s at rank 1 and only lets her dash if the shuriken actually connects.
audit.corrected: Twilight Shroud 20/19/18/17/16. Shuriken Flip 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 and must hit to enable the dash. Inside shroud she cannot be targeted by Blinding Dart; existing Toxic Shot ticks continue.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akali.json — W '20/19/18/17/16', E '16/14.5/13/11.5/10', W 'unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks'

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 1-2 advice is 'don't force it' with no mechanical reason a Teemo can act on, and Akali's resource is never mentioned.
audit.why: Akali is on Energy with a 200 pool, and Five Point Strike costs 110 at rank 1. Two Qs cost 220, so she physically cannot cast it twice from full — after one Q she is at 90 energy and, with Shuriken Flip at 30 on top, she is dry. That is a hard, countable second trade window, and it turns a vague 'respect her' into something a player can time.
audit.corrected: Five Point Strike costs 110 energy of a 200 pool at rank 1 — she cannot double-Q. The trade after her first Q is free.

edits.before: Akali wins levels 1 and 2 cleanly. Her passive Mark stacks off her own Q and any auto, and she can trade back onto you before your E poison has time to deliver meaningful damage — she is not a pure auto-trader you can just blind and walk away from. Do not try to prove anything pre-level 3: last-hit at the tip of AA range, keep a poison stack ticking if she steps up, and most importantly identify when her Twilight Shroud is on cooldown before you commit a single step forward. She cannot trade through a blind IF she has already used W, so your whole early-game job is forcing her to spend that button on poke rather than a kill attempt.
edits.after: Akali wins levels 1 and 2 cleanly. Assassin's Mark comes off her spell damage, never her autos: she Qs you, walks out of the ring it draws, and her next basic attack gains bonus range and damage — that exit step is your cue to hold Blinding Dart, because the empowered hit is a basic attack and blind deletes it. Five Point Strike also costs 110 energy of a 200 pool, so she cannot chain two of them; the trade immediately after her first Q is the free one. Do not force anything pre-level 3: last-hit at the tip of AA range, keep a poison stack ticking, and know whether Twilight Shroud is down before you step forward.

edits.before: Levels 3 through 5 are the contested window where this lane can swing either direction. Your Q is approaching max rank, your shrooms are cheap enough to drop on every bush approach, and Twilight Shroud has a real 25-second cooldown you can exploit. The pattern: auto-poke her whenever she steps to a minion, blind her when she retaliates, and immediately walk backward out of her Q range. If she burns W to dodge a blind, that is your full commitment window — run your entire pattern while she is visible and grounded. Shroom the tribush and both side bushes so her approach paths are permanently lit; she cannot enter your half of the lane unseen, and any attempt to walk through a shroom burns her W or eats a slow that lets you kite to tower.
